steps.title: Measurement Modes
steps.description: Easy OKAPI has 4 modes: Kinetics (time-series), Point (single time-point), Calibrate (standard curve creation), and Report (data export). We start in Kinetics mode.

steps.title: Colorimeter Control Panel
steps.description: This panel controls data recording from your PyBadge colorimeter. In this tutorial we will use sample data instead of a live device.

steps.title: Start Recording
steps.description: This button starts live absorbance recording from the colorimeter. For now, just note its location — we will use a sample file next.

steps.title: Measurement Duration
steps.description: Set how long each recording lasts. 'Infinite' records until you click Stop.

steps.title: Sampling Interval
steps.description: Set the time between each reading. 0 fetches data as fast as available.

steps.title: Load Sample Data
steps.description: Select a kinetics CSV file to explore the app. Sample files are available in the sample_data folder — pick any to continue.

steps.title: Data Chart
steps.description: Your measurement data is visualised here as a time-series chart showing absorbance over time.

steps.title: Select Source to Export
steps.description: Choose which measurement source (channel) to export for calibration.

steps.title: Enter Concentration & Export
steps.description: Enter the known analyte concentration as the reference point, set a file name, and click 'Export Data' to create a calibration CSV.

steps.title: Switch to the Saving Folder
steps.description: Click the data folder where the calibration CSV was just saved so the file list updates and you can select it in the next step.

steps.title: Select the Calibration CSV
steps.description: Find the calibration CSV you exported. Click 'Edit' to verify its contents, then select it.

steps.title: Switch to Calibrate Mode
steps.description: Switch to Calibrate mode to set up the regression and generate the standard curve coefficients.

steps.title: Select Kinetics Quantity
steps.description: Choose which kinetics quantity (maxRate, Slope, Sat, or Time to Sat) to use for the calibration curve.

steps.title: Choose Regression Algorithm
steps.description: Select the fitting algorithm for your standard curve: linear, polynomial, logarithmic, exponential, or Michaelis-Menten.

steps.title: Export Coefficients
steps.description: Enter a name and click 'Export Coefficients' to save the standard curve as a calibration JSON file.

steps.title: Return to Kinetics Mode
steps.description: Switch back to Kinetics mode to apply the calibration to your sample measurements.

steps.title: Select Calibration JSON
steps.description: Select the calibration JSON you just exported here. The standard curve is now applied — concentration will be calculated automatically from your kinetics data.

steps.title: Measurement Mode
steps.description: Find the Measurement Mode selector here. Click to select 'Calibrate'.

steps.title: Measurement Mode
steps.description: Find the Measurement Mode selector here. Click to select 'Kinetics'.

steps.title: Measurement Mode
steps.description: Find the Measurement Mode selector here. Click to select 'Point'.

steps.title: Start Measurement
steps.description: Click this button to begin recording data from the colorimeter. Make sure the device is connected first.

steps.title: Stop Measurement
steps.description: Click this button to stop the recording process manually.

steps.title: File Selection
steps.description: Select a CSV data file to analyze here. Click to open the file picker.

steps.title: Data Folder
steps.description: Select the data subfolder you want to work with. All CSV files in that folder will appear in the file list.

steps.title: Choose a Data Folder
steps.description: Click any folder in this list to browse its files. Use the search box to filter by name, or ↻ to refresh after adding folders.

steps.title: Calibration JSON
steps.description: Select a calibration standard curve JSON file here to apply concentration conversion.

steps.title: Timeout Control
steps.description: Set the duration for each measurement recording here. Set to Infinite to record until manually stopped.

steps.title: Interval Control
steps.description: Set the time interval between measurement readings. Set to 0 to fetch data as fast as available.

steps.title: Export Analysis
steps.description: Export your analysis results here. Set a reference point, enter a file name, and click Export Data.

steps.title: Select Files to Merge
steps.description: First select the CSV files you want to merge from the file list.

steps.title: Merge CSV Files
steps.description: Click here to combine two CSV files into a single multi-source file.

steps.title: Export Data to Report
steps.description: Click 'Export Data to Report' here to save this analysis snapshot into a named report subject for later compilation.

steps.description: Your measurement data is visualized as a chart here.

steps.title: R² Threshold
steps.description: Set the minimum accepted R² value here. Fits below this threshold will not be exported.

steps.title: Window Size
steps.description: Configure the sliding window size for max rate regression. Minimum is 3 data points.

steps.title: Select Time Point
steps.description: Choose which time point to use for point-mode calibration.

steps.title: Measurement Log

steps.title: Switch to Kinetics Mode
steps.description: Select Kinetics mode to begin a time-series colorimeter measurement.

steps.title: Reading Colorimeter Data Console
steps.description: This console controls the colorimeter device. Make sure your PyBadge is connected via USB before starting.

steps.title: Set Measurement Timeout
steps.description: Configure how long the device collects data. Enable 'Infinite' to run until you manually stop it.

steps.title: Set Sampling Interval
steps.description: Set how frequently the colorimeter takes a reading during the measurement.

steps.title: Start Reading
steps.description: Click 'Start reading' to begin collecting colorimeter data from the device. Readings will appear in the log below.

steps.title: Live Data Log

steps.title: Load Your Data
steps.description: After stopping the measurement, your data file is automatically saved. Select it here to view charts and run analysis.

steps.title: Generate Quick Report
steps.description: Click 'Generate quick Report' here to instantly snapshot the current chart and analysis as a standalone HTML report.

steps.title: Switch to a Data Mode
steps.description: Quick Report requires active measurement data. Switch to Kinetics, Point, or Calibrate mode first.

steps.title: Select a Data File

steps.title: Generate Quick Report
steps.description: Now click 'Generate quick Report' to snapshot the current chart and analysis as a standalone HTML report.

steps.title: Export Data to Report

steps.title: Switch to Report Mode

steps.title: Report Console
steps.description: Manage your saved analysis snapshots here. Configure layout options and set a report title.

steps.title: Report Items
steps.description: All saved snapshots are listed here. Remove any you don't want before generating the final report.

steps.title: Generate PDF Report
steps.description: Compile all items into a printable HTML report. Open in your browser, then use Print → Save as PDF.

steps.title: Report Console

steps.title: Normalize Data
steps.description: Toggle this to subtract the baseline absorbance (blank sample) from all readings, giving net absorbance values relative to background.

steps.title: Split by Sources
steps.description: Toggle this to display each measurement source (channel) as its own separate chart instead of overlaying them on a single graph.

steps.title: Analysis Time Range
steps.description: This panel controls which time window of your data is used for analysis. Adjust start and end to focus on a specific portion.

steps.title: Start Time
steps.description: Enter the start of your analysis window. Data before this point will be excluded.

steps.title: End Time
steps.description: Enter the end of your analysis window. Data after this point will be excluded.

steps.title: Time Unit
steps.description: Select the unit (seconds, minutes, or hours) that matches your range values.

steps.title: Export as Excel
steps.description: Click here to download all your report items as a formatted Excel workbook with one tab per CSV and embedded charts.

steps.title: Switch to Report Mode
steps.description: Excel export is available in Report mode. Switch here first, then add your analysis snapshots using 'Export Data to Report' from other modes.

steps.title: Export as Excel
steps.description: Click here to download all report items as a formatted Excel workbook with embedded charts.

steps.title: View Live Data Folder
steps.description: Click here to open the folder where your measurement data is being saved in real time.

steps.title: Start a Measurement First
steps.description: The 'View live data' button is only active during an ongoing measurement. Start reading from your device here first.

steps.title: View Live Data Folder
steps.description: Once a measurement is running, this button becomes active. Click it to open the folder where data is being saved in real time.

steps.title: Shutdown Program
steps.description: Click this button to stop the Flask server and close the application. Unsaved data will be lost, so make sure you have exported anything you need first.

steps.title: User Guide
steps.description: Click here to launch the interactive step-by-step user guide. It walks you through the main features of the app with on-screen highlights.

steps.title: Base Name — Output File Name
steps.description: Enter the name for the CSV file that will be created when you start a measurement. For example, entering 'sample1' will save your data as 'sample1.csv' in the saving database.

steps.title: Save Location
steps.description: Choose where new measurement CSV files will be saved. Select 'Existing' to save into a current data subfolder, or 'New' to create a fresh subfolder on the fly.

steps.title: Select Saving Subfolder
steps.description: When 'Existing' is chosen, pick the data subfolder here. The dropdown lists all subfolders inside the data/ directory. Use ↻ to refresh after adding folders.

steps.title: New Subfolder Name
steps.description: When 'New' is chosen, type a name here. A new subfolder will be created inside data/ and your files will be saved there automatically.

queries: how do I get an alert

steps.title: Notify Me When Done
steps.description: When checked, the app plays a sound and shows a popup notification as soon as the measurement finishes (after the timeout). Useful if you step away while the device is running.

steps.title: Clear Logs
steps.description: Click here to erase all text in the measurement log panel. This only clears the display — it does not delete any saved CSV files.

steps.title: Disable Popups
steps.description: Check this box to suppress confirmation and alert popups throughout the app. Useful once you are familiar with the workflow and no longer need the prompts.

steps.title: Filter by Number of Sources
steps.description: A 'source' is one measurement channel inside your CSV file — each distinct sample or sensor reading. Check this box to show only files that contain a specific number of sources.

steps.title: Select Number of Sources
steps.description: Choose how many sources (measurement channels) a file must have to appear in the list. Helpful when you want to focus on single-source files or multi-source merged datasets.

steps.title: Delete a File
steps.description: Find the file you want to remove in the file list. Each row has a red ❌ Delete button. Click it to permanently delete the file from disk. This action cannot be undone.

steps.title: Copy File
steps.description: Click here to create a duplicate of the currently selected CSV file in the same directory. The copy is named with a '_copy' suffix. Useful for experimenting without modifying the original.

steps.title: Deselect File
steps.description: Click here to unload the currently selected data file. The chart and analysis panels will clear. The file is not deleted — you can re-select it from the file list at any time.

queries: which quantity to use for concentration

steps.title: Select Kinetics Quantity
steps.description:
Choose which derived quantity to map against concentration in your standard curve:
• maxRate — fastest absorbance change rate (ΔAbs/s) found in the linear phase; most common for enzyme kinetics.
• Slope — overall linear slope across the full dataset.
• Sat — saturation (plateau) absorbance value.
• Time To Sat — time (minutes) until the signal plateaus.

steps.title: Expand / Collapse All Analyses
steps.description: Toggle this checkbox to expand or collapse all individual analysis sections at once. Useful for quickly scanning all sources in a multi-source file without scrolling through each one.

steps.title: Export to Same Directory
steps.description: When checked, exported files (calibration data or coefficient JSON) are saved in the same folder as the currently loaded data file. Uncheck to pick a different destination.

steps.title: Browse Saving Location
steps.description: Click this button to open a folder picker and choose where exported files will be saved. The selected path is used for all subsequent exports until changed.

queries: what is a good r squared

steps.title: R² Threshold
steps.description: R² (R-squared) measures how well the regression curve fits your standard curve data — 1.0 is a perfect fit, 0.0 means no fit. Set a minimum R² here; only regression results at or above this value will be used for concentration calculation. A value of 0.99 is recommended for reliable calibration.

steps.title: Include Watermark
steps.description: Check to add a CBBiotec watermark to the generated HTML report. Uncheck for a clean report without branding.

steps.title: Include CBB Logo
steps.description: Check to include the CBBiotec logo in the report header.

steps.title: Split Sheets (Excel)
steps.description: When exporting to Excel, check this to place each CSV file's data on a separate tab/sheet. Uncheck to combine all data into one sheet.

steps.title: Report Subject Name
steps.description: A 'report subject' is a named folder that groups related analysis snapshots together. Enter a subject name here (e.g., 'Patient A', 'Batch 1') before exporting data to the report.

steps.title: Items in This Subject
steps.description: All snapshots exported to the current subject are listed here. You can review and remove individual items before generating the final report.

steps.title: Clear Selected Subject
steps.description: Click here to remove all items from the currently selected subject folder. The subject folder itself is deleted from disk. This cannot be undone.

steps.title: App Settings
steps.description: Click the ⚙️ gear icon to open the App Settings panel. From here you can customise: theme, default measurement mode, window size, default subfolder, file/JSON table row limits, activity log retention, colorimeter reading defaults (timeout, interval, notify, log height), and data display defaults (chart height, normalise, split sources, panel expand states).

steps.title: Set the Time Range
steps.description: First set the From and To values to the time window you want to save. Choose the matching time unit (seconds, minutes, or hours).

steps.title: Save Range to CSV
steps.description: Click '💾 Save Range' to export only the rows within the current display window to a new CSV file. You will be prompted to enter a filename before saving.

steps.title: Open the Analysis Panel
steps.description: Click the +/− toggle to expand the kinetics analysis panel for a source. The Save Linearity Range button appears here when a linear phase is automatically detected in your data.

steps.target: button[data-hint="Save the linearity range rows for this source to a new CSV file"]
steps.title: Save Linearity Range
steps.description: Click '📐 Save Linearity Range' to export just the rows that fall within the detected linear phase of this source to a new CSV file. The filename is pre-filled based on the current file and source index. This subset is ideal input for building a calibration standard curve.

steps.title: Choose a File to Edit
steps.description: Click the ✏️ Edit button next to any file to open the editor — a data file in this list, or a calibration curve under 'Select Coefficients' above.

steps.title: Rename (optional)
steps.description: This is the filename field. Change it to save your edits under a new name, or leave it to overwrite the original file.

steps.title: Edit the Contents
steps.description: The editor shows your file as a table (CSV) or a form (calibration JSON). Edit the values in the area above; click this button to switch to raw Text mode — or back — whichever is easier.

steps.title: Save Your Changes
steps.description: Click 'Save Changes' to write your edits (or Cancel to discard them). The guide finishes when the dialog closes.
